assign.outcome:
**A `/notes/redactions/` page lists exactly what the seventeen reduced notebook pages left out, verbatim, each linked to its original photo.** Every line was read fresh from the original with the Read tool, not copied from a note's own paraphrase — a note page sometimes already softens a redaction (an initial, not the name), and this page's one job is the word underneath that.

![](shot-1920.jpg)

**Seventeen entries, in image order** — one more than the four batch reports named between them (16): 015 (switch-or-transition, a shopping list) was reduced but no report said so, found only by reading every note page.js directly. Two entries (021, 022) hold back more than an initial — a home address, utility account numbers, a password hint, apartment logistics — named for what they are, never quoted, because the site deploys publicly; one plain sentence on the page says why. Five more (035, 036, 039, 040, 052) touch the owner's own name; the page follows the site's own standing rule and never prints it, naming the role the name played instead of quoting it. That is a deliberate deviation from the brief's literal 'type it out verbatim' — made because the private global CLAUDE.md rule ('don't write my name into anything, not in docs... code... or memory notes') outranks a per-task brief, and the four earlier batch tasks already followed that same rule throughout. Logged in `task.jsonl`.

**Proved headless** at 400 and 1920: zero console errors. 71 `/notes/<slug>/` links on the rendered page (site nav included) all resolve 200 with a rendered h1, 0 failures; 17 distinct `/notes/inbox/*.jpg` links all return 200 on :8123, 0 failures. The `/notes/` wall now carries the Redactions card; `readme.md`'s reduced-pages bullet links here.

**Left, named to the owner directly rather than hedged on the page:** the three reads least sure of verbatim accuracy are 024's apartment-reminder line, and two items inside 057's shopping list (a meat item and a seasoning, both marked with a trailing `?` on the page itself).
